test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 23 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following DRDO-executed schemes under the ‘Make in India’ initiative provides grants-in-aid to Indian industries (MSMEs/start-ups) for developing defence and dual-use technologies?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Technology Development Fund (TDF)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Technology Development Fund (TDF)** is a flagship program of the **Ministry of Defence**, executed specifically by the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** under the **‘Make in India’** initiative.
 
• The primary objective of the **TDF scheme** is to provide **grants-in-aid** to **Indian industries**, including **MSMEs** and **start-ups**, to encourage the design and development of indigenous **defence and dual-use technologies**.
 
• The scheme aims to bridge the gap between R&D and commercialization by supporting the development of **prototypes** or upgrading existing systems to meet the requirements of the **Indian Armed Forces**.
 
• Under this program, the **DRDO** provides financial support up to **90%** of the total project cost. In **June 2022**, the funding limit was significantly enhanced from **₹10 crore** to **₹50 crore** per project to accommodate high-value technology development.
 
• The program is designed to foster a culture of **innovation** and **self-reliance (Aatmanirbharta)** in the defence sector by involving private sector players in cutting-edge technology domains.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Innovations for Defence Excellence (iDEX):**
 
 
• Launched in **April 2018**, **iDEX** is aimed at creating an ecosystem to foster innovation and technology development in **Defence and Aerospace**.
 
• It is funded and managed by the **Defence Innovation Organisation (DIO)**, not directly by DRDO.
 
• It provides a platform for **start-ups**, **individual innovators**, and **MSMEs** to solve challenges posed by the Services through the **Defence India Start-up Challenge (DISC)**.
 
 
 
• **Defence Testing Infrastructure Scheme (DTIS):**
 
 
• Launched in **May 2020** with an outlay of **₹400 crore**, this scheme focuses on creating state-of-the-art **testing facilities** in partnership with the private sector.
 
• It aims to promote indigenous production by providing **Greenfield Testing Infrastructure**, particularly in the **Defence Industrial Corridors** of **Uttar Pradesh** and **Tamil Nadu**.
 
 
 
• **Aatmanirbhar Defence Innovation & Technology Initiative (ADITI):**
 
 
• Launched in **March 2024**, **ADITI** is a specialized scheme under the **iDEX** framework to promote **deep-tech** innovations in the defence sector.
 
• It offers grants-in-aid up to **₹25 crore** to eligible start-ups for research and development in critical and strategic technology areas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Eligibility for TDF:** Only **Indian companies** incorporated under the **Companies Act 2013** or **LLP Act 2008** are eligible. The majority stake (at least **51%**) must be held by **Indian citizens**.
 
• **Dual-use Technology:** These are technologies like **advanced sensors**, **AI-based surveillance**, and **drones** that have applications in both **military warfare** and **civilian sectors** (e.g., disaster management or logistics).
 
• **Project Duration:** The maximum development period for a project under the **TDF** is generally **2 years**, ensuring a fast-track approach to technology indigenization.
 
• **Nodal Agency:** While the **Ministry of Defence** provides the mandate, the **Directorate of TDF** within **DRDO** acts as the nodal agency for evaluation and implementation.
